summary: Ran `npx -y -p @angular/cli@21 ng update @angular/core@21 @angular/cli@21 --allow-dirty --force` from EFNgApp/EFNgApp/ClientApp on Node 22/npm 10, bumping @angular/* to 21.2.26, the CLI/build-angular toolchain to 21.2.30, @angular/compiler-cli and @angular/language-service to 21.2.26, and TypeScript to ~5.9.3. The update's mandatory migrations updated tsconfig.json's `lib` entry (dropped the explicit `es2017`/`dom` list now that the compiler infers a modern default from `target`), migrated src/main.ts's bootstrap options to the new `provideZoneChangeDetection()` provider, and converted the three templates still using `*ngIf`/`*ngFor` (add-employee, fetch-data, fetch-employee) to the new `@if`/`@for` block control-flow syntax. The hop file listed no related packages needing a bump, but `npm install` with legacy-peer-deps masked a real peer mismatch: @ngrx/* was still on ^20.1.0, whose packages peer-depend on `@angular/core: ^20.0.0`. Bumped all five @ngrx/* packages to ^21.1.1 (first @ngrx major with an `@angular/core: ^21.0.0` peer range) to keep the dependency graph internally consistent, matching the pattern from the previous hop. Install and build both pass; test fails the same pre-existing way as baseline and every prior hop (angular.json's test target points at root-level styles.css instead of src/styles.css, unchanged by this hop).
changes: @angular/cli migration: removed the now-redundant explicit `lib` array from tsconfig.json (modern default lib is inferred from `target: ES2022`)
@angular/core migration: migrated src/main.ts's bootstrapModule options to use `provideZoneChangeDetection()`

@angular/core migration: converted `*ngIf`/`*ngFor` structural directives to `@if`/`@for` block control-flow syntax in src/app/add-employee/add-employee.component.html, src/app/fetch-data/fetch-data.component.html and src/app/fetch-employee/fetch-employee.component.html

Upgraded @ngrx/effects, @ngrx/entity, @ngrx/router-store, @ngrx/store and @ngrx/store-devtools from ^20.1.0 to ^21.1.1, since their Angular 20 peer range (`@angular/core: ^20.0.0`) no longer matches the app's Angular 21; the hop's automated dependency detection missed this because legacy-peer-deps suppresses the npm peer-dependency error
package-lock.json regenerated by npm as part of the update/install cycles
manual_followups: npm install still needs legacy-peer-deps (set project-wide via ClientApp/.npmrc in an earlier hop) because @nguniversal/module-map-ngfactory-loader@7.1.0 declares peers on an old @angular/* major; it should be replaced by @angular/ssr (the @nguniversal scope was merged into @angular/ssr from Angular 17 onward) in a follow-up. The .npmrc override can likely be removed once that is resolved.

`npm run test` fails before any spec executes because angular.json's test architect target still points at `styles.css` at the ClientApp root instead of `src/styles.css`; this predates this hop (present since baseline) and was left as-is per the rule that pre-existing failures don't need fixing.

This is the final hop (Angular 8 to 21). The optional 'use-application-builder' migration (moving from the webpack-based builder to the new esbuild/vite-based application builder) was not applied, kept out of scope in the previous hop to keep changes minimal and still worth a dedicated follow-up pass outside this upgrade chain.
